text: The model flagged this applicant as high‑risk because three key signals pushed the default probability above 50 %. First, the revolving‑credit utilization is essentially 100 % (0.9999999), and this alone added about 1.4 points to the risk score, indicating the applicant is using almost all of the credit that’s available. Second, there is one account that is 30‑59 days past due; that contributed roughly 0.5 points, showing a recent payment slip‑up. Finally, the applicant has no open credit lines or loans, which actually reduced risk a little (‑0.34 points), but the reduction was far outweighed by the high utilization and the past‑due account. Together, these factors led the model to assign a 54.5 % probability of default and label the case as HIGH RISK.
